title: Out of Sight Out of Mind: Measuring Bias in Language Models Against Overlooked Marginalized Groups in Regional Contexts

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting language models with sentence templates containing male, female, and non-binary identity terms, then measuring toxic sentence probabilities (SOS score) and the generation of hurtful words (HONEST score).
Substituting LGBTQIA+ identity terms into toxic and non-toxic sentence templates to evaluate offensive stereotyping and the percentage of hurtful lexicon words generated by the models.

Measuring offensive stereotyping by replacing placeholders in templates with inclusive language terms describing people with disabilities and calculating the pseudo-log-likelihood of toxic associations.
Comparing model outputs across regionally specific ethnic minority and dominant groups by substituting their names into templates and evaluating toxicity probabilities and hurtful word completions.

Analyzing bias related to power dynamics by substituting specific refugee group identities (e.g., Syrians, Afghans) into templates and comparing their offensive stereotyping scores against national dominant groups in Germany and Egypt.
Evaluating language models on templates containing regional minority and dominant religious identities to assess the percentage of generated hurtful words and the likelihood of toxic contexts.
Combining gender terms (male, female, non-binary) with other sensitive attributes (e.g., Black women, LGBTQIA+ women) in sentence templates to evaluate compounded offensive stereotyping bias.
